rationale.conceptual: The method uses standard GCMC with common force fields (UFF, TraPPE, TIP3P) and a well-known selectivity formula; it is a direct application of established simulation techniques, requiring no novel algorithm or deep domain insight beyond configuring a standard workflow.
rationale.execution: The pipeline involves many sequential stages: obtaining crystal structures, running DFT for charges, assembling force field files, and performing numerous GCMC simulations (pure ethanol, pure water, mixture across four ZIFs, two temperatures, and multiple pressures) followed by post-processing. It requires fragile multi-tool orchestration (CSD or RCSR, DFT code, GCMC engine like RASPA) and careful management of many interdependent simulation tasks.

difficulty.reasoning: The paper applies standard Grand Canonical Monte Carlo simulations with well-known force fields to study adsorption in ZIFs. The method is an off-the-shelf application of established computational chemistry techniques, leading to a low conceptual difficulty. However, reproducing the results requires a multi-stage pipeline with fragile tooling (DFT, GCMC engine, data retrieval), many simulation runs, and complex orchestration, resulting in high execution difficulty.

compute_estimate.reasoning: All calculations are CPU-only (DFT on small unit cells, GCMC on modest supercells). Memory needs are modest; input data (crystal structures, force field parameters, charges) are tiny. No GPU is required.
